summary: An indologist and historian/archaeologist, Michael Haberlandt earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1878–1882) under Friedrich Müller and Georg Bühler. He served at the University of Vienna as PD (1892) and ao. Professor (1910), and directed the Natural History Museum, Vienna (1911).

Michael Hahn, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (1965–1967) under Wilhelm Rau. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (from 1974) and the University of Marburg (1976–1980, 1988–2007).
Working in religious studies and sinology, Michael Harack completed his Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).
Michael Hookham, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt, an Indologist and linguist, earned a BA at SOAS (~1976–1980) and a doctorate at the University of London (~1980–1984). He held posts at SOAS as British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow (1987), Emeritus Professor (1995–1999), and Associate Dean (2002–2010).

Specializing in religious studies, Japanology, and Sinology, Michael I. Como studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He held appointments at Columbia University, including as Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies (attested 2026).

Michael J. Sweet worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He later served as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1994–2006).
Michael J. Tetreault, a scholar in religious studies and philosophy, completed his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).

Michael J. Walsh works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town (~1986–1989), earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara (~1992–1994), and completed his doctorate there under William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

Michael Janda, a linguist and Indologist, earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (~1990–1996) under Heiner Eichner and completed his Habilitation at Zurich (~1996–1999). He was an assistant at Zurich (1995) and held a chair at Münster (2002).

An archaeology and Indology scholar, Michael Jansen completed his doctorate at RWTH Aachen University (~1967–1979). He served as Dean of Architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999) and founding rector of the German University of Technology in Oman (2007–2008).

Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at UC Santa Barbara (~2003–2008) under Mark Juergensmeyer. He taught at Eckerd College (~2009–2012) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Michael Kowalewski studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter, who studied under Larry William Moses, worked in Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Indiana University Bloomington as an Editorial Consultant (attested 1982) and Special Languages Cataloger (attested 2020).

Michael Lessman, an Indology and religious studies scholar, earned degrees from Georgetown (BA 2010–2014), Catholic University of America (MA 2014–2017), and University of Munich (MA 2017–2019). He became a doctoral candidate at Yale University in 2019.

Michael M. Ames, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1956–1961) under Cora Du Bois. He taught at McMaster University (1962–1964) and UBC (from 1964), later serving as Director of UBC's Museum of Anthropology (1974–1997).
Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1962–1968) and held a post at the University of Oxford.
Linguist Michael Meier-Brügger studied under Ernst Risch at the University of Zurich (~1967–1973) and later held a post at the Free University of Berlin (~1996–2013).
Michael Oppitz, working in Tibetology and other fields, held a post at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as Leiter at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).

Michael Pakenham Edgeworth was an Indology scholar who studied at Charterhouse School and the University of Edinburgh (~1827–1829). He served in the Indian Civil Service as a civil servant from 1831 to 1859.
